title: James Beveridge, Marblehead and the Fort Richmond migration
observation: The family book describes an earlier James coming from Scotland, a son James born in 1724, and a move to Fort Richmond in the 1730s. The author explicitly presents the indentured-servant idea as a probability rather than a documented fact.
status: Published family narrative; immigrant identity and service unverified
verification: OCR navigation lead; inspect displayed original scanned page
why_it_matters: The immigrant-generation bridge is still missing and this account cannot establish an emigrant's Scottish parents.
next_originals: Original Marblehead birth register for 1724 James and parent names
Fort Richmond muster/pay rolls naming the elder James, with service dates and identifying features
Scotland-to-Marblehead migration documents with matching identity

title: Jean McKinney White, James Jr., and the Fox Islands migration
observation: The narrative identifies Jean as Nicholas White's widow, names George and John as her children, and describes Thomas as born while James and Jean lived near the Minot stockade. It reports Thomas's move to the Fox Islands about 1771.
status: Published retrospective account; identities and marriage solemnization not independently proved
verification: OCR navigation lead; inspect displayed original scanned page
why_it_matters: The 1748/9 Brunswick register has a marriage intention, not independently checked solemnization; George and John's parentage requires original records.
next_originals: Brunswick/Georgetown original marriage return and intention pages
Probate or military record naming Nicholas White and his surviving family
Original Fort Richmond/Topsham land or baptism records naming Thomas and his parents

title: Thomas and Mercy Kent, 1774 Boston, and the Tea Party family story
observation: The original printed page names the reported Boston marriage date of 13 April 1774 and distinguishes the family's Boston Tea Party story from a documented participant listing. The author observes the family story lacks a surviving proof of Thomas's participation.
status: Page visually inspected: memoir reports family tradition and an unverified ceremony date
verification: Visually compared directly with original book page
why_it_matters: Preserve the existing Boston Tea Party claim as family tradition without silently upgrading it to an established event or deleting it.
next_originals: Contemporary Boston marriage return for Thomas and Mercy on or around 13 April 1774
Independent 1773/1774 participant or residence evidence, if surviving
Earliest dated family account documenting when the Tea Party tradition arose

title: Matthew's first and second wives: the 1865 family register clarifies the apparent conflict
observation: The 2016 book calls Matthew a younger brother of Thomas and reports Matthew's Abigail Dyer marriage in 1801. An earlier near-contemporary source, Cyrus Eaton's 1865 Thomaston/Rockland family register (vol. II, p.146), explicitly describes one Capt. Matthew Beverage of Hope marrying Abigail Dyer first and Clarissa Cobb second; it allocates five named children to each wife. These published accounts are compatible on the Abigail marriage, not evidence of two different Matthews by themselves.
status: The earlier apparent first-wife/second-wife contradiction is resolved WITHIN Eaton's published account; original marriage certificates and identity with Thomas's brother remain unverified
verification: Visually compared directly with original book page
why_it_matters: Corrects the earlier misleading two-Matthews conflict without inventing a civil marriage certificate. Eaton's marriage order is explicit; his parents, the 1785 minor's identity, and Matthew's exact connection to Thomas and Nathaniel still need independent original records.
next_originals: Original Matthew–Abigail Dyer marriage entry around 1801 to check the book's stated date
Original Matthew–Clarissa Cobb marriage entry and 1830s Hope estate/probate naming widow and children
Original identity bridge from 1785 Fox Islands minor Matthew to Capt. Matthew and the claimed Thomas brotherhood

supporting_source.title: Cyrus Eaton, History of Thomaston/Rockland (1865), vol. II p.146
supporting_source.locator: BEVERAGE, Capt. Matthew, wife order and two five-child groups

title: 1787 James death and the Fox Islands return
observation: The narrative reports that Thomas, Mercy, their three eldest children, Thomas's father James and younger brother Matthew returned after the Revolutionary War; the elder James reportedly died on the islands in 1787.
status: Page visually inspected; father-son identification not independently proved by this passage
verification: Visually compared directly with original book page
why_it_matters: A reported 1787 death is not yet a parent-naming probate or proof that the Fort Richmond and Fox Islands men are the same James.
next_originals: North Haven/Vinalhaven early death record and burial documentation for James in 1787
Original 1786 sworn testimony and 1781 travel-pass evidence to identify the relevant James
Probate or land succession naming the decedent's children

title: 1785 town clerk and land-petition narrative
observation: The book reports that Thomas was elected town clerk in March 1785 and that George White acted for the settlers in a petition for clear land title; the page describes related settlement and return to the islands.
status: Published account; original town minutes and signed petition not inspected for this note
verification: OCR navigation lead; compare against original book page
why_it_matters: This points to a separate post-war petition and local original minute book; do not conflate it with the December 1763 Topsham incorporation petition.
next_originals: March 1785 original Fox Islands meeting minutes and clerk appointment
Exact dated General Court petition manuscript or filed copy
Contemporary land grants, including acreage and grantee names

title: Reproduced settlers' petition facsimile
observation: The book contains a photographed or reproduced printed image of a Fox Islands settlers' petition. Its typography is difficult for OCR; any transcription must be checked visually and traced to its originating archive.
status: Facsimile in family book; archival original and date not authenticated
verification: OCR unreliable for facsimile; original-page visual inspection required
why_it_matters: A picture of a petition in a modern book is not automatically an authenticated original signature or complete historical transcription.
next_originals: Identify repository, collection, folio and date of reproduced petition
Inspect an archival image at high resolution and compare legible names
Determine whether labels are original signatures or a copied list

title: The Grant family's separate Scottish ancestry story
observation: The book recounts a collateral Grant family tradition tracing back to a Peter Grant associated with prisoners after the Battle of Dunbar in 1650 and later work at Lynn Iron Works; this is distinct from verifying a Beveridge immigrant's Scottish origin.
status: Published collateral-family narrative; eighteenth- and seventeenth-century identities need original chain
verification: OCR navigation lead; compare against original book page
why_it_matters: Scottish surname parallels must not be used as proof that the unrelated Beveridge ancestor came from the same military context.
next_originals: Contemporary Lynn Iron Works indenture/ownership and transport records
Original Grant birth/marriage/probate chain to Amelia Beverage
Distinguish Peter Grant prison-tradition documentation from later compiled ancestry
